name: East India Company
description: English joint-stock company that became a territorial power in India.

name: Robert Clive
description: Company officer and victor at Plassey; later Governor of Bengal.

name: Warren Hastings
description: First Governor-General of Bengal; impeached 1787 and acquitted 1795.

name: Mir Jafar
description: Commander who aided the Company at Plassey and became Nawab of Bengal.

name: British Parliament
description: Legislature that regulated and eventually absorbed the Company.

name: British Crown
description: Assumed direct rule of India in 1858.

name: Anglo-Iranian Oil Company (later BP)
description: British oil company whose Iranian concession was nationalized in 1951.

name: Mohammad Mossadegh
description: Prime Minister of Iran 1951-1953.

name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
description: Shah of Iran, restored to full power after the 1953 coup.

name: Central Intelligence Agency
description: US agency that planned and directed Operation Ajax.

name: MI6 (Secret Intelligence Service)
description: British agency that co-planned the coup (Operation Boot).

name: Kermit Roosevelt Jr.
description: CIA officer who led the field operation in Tehran.

name: Fazlollah Zahedi
description: General installed as prime minister after the coup.

name: Government of Iran
description: Nationalized the oil industry in 1951.

name: Allen W. Dulles
description: Director of Central Intelligence from 1953 to 1961; brother of John Foster Dulles.

name: John Foster Dulles
description: US Secretary of State, 1953–1959; brother of Allen W. Dulles.

name: US Department of State
description: US foreign-policy department led by John Foster Dulles during the 1953 Iran crisis.

name: George Grenville
description: British prime minister whose ministry pursued postwar colonial revenue and the 1765 Stamp Act.

name: Thomas Hutchinson
description: Royal governor of Massachusetts; his two sons were designated tea consignees. The family tie alone does not establish that he arranged their appointment.

name: First Continental Congress
description: Assembly of representatives from British mainland North American colonies convened in Philadelphia in September 1774 to coordinate grievances and responses to British policy.

name: Boston tea protest movement
description: Colonial organizers and participants opposing tea policy in Boston; not a single uniform organization or ideology.

name: Pontiac
description: Ottawa leader associated with a coordinated Indigenous resistance movement against British military posts and settler expansion after the Seven Years' War.

name: Virginia colonial land investors
description: A category of land speculators and companies seeking western territorial claims, rather than a single coordinated body.

name: Massachusetts colonial militias
description: Locally organized militia companies that opposed British regular troops at Lexington and Concord in April 1775.

name: Frederick North (Lord North)
description: British prime minister during the Tea Act and East India Company's 1773 financial crisis.

name: Richard Clarke
description: Boston merchant and senior member of Richard Clarke & Sons, a 1773 tea-consignee firm.

name: Richard Clarke & Sons
description: Boston mercantile firm selected to receive East India Company tea; a commercial role, not itself evidence of payment realized.

name: Thomas Hutchinson Jr.
description: Son of Governor Thomas Hutchinson; selected as a Boston tea consignee in 1773.

name: Elisha Hutchinson
description: Son of Governor Thomas Hutchinson; selected as a Boston tea consignee in 1773.

name: Joshua Winslow
description: Massachusetts merchant and East India Company tea consignee whose November 18 1773 letter discussed a prospective commission.

name: Benjamin Faneuil Jr.
description: Partner of Joshua Winslow in a Boston firm selected to receive East India Company tea.

name: Brook Watson
description: London merchant who recommended Joshua Winslow and Benjamin Faneuil Jr. as tea consignees, according to Massachusetts Commonwealth Museum.

name: Jotham Gay
description: Merchant and correspondent who received Joshua Winslow's November 18 1773 letter about tea consignment.

name: Bank of England
description: Banking institution whose archive preserves a March 1766 note concerning an existing £50,000 loan to the East India Company.

name: Henry Crabb Boulton
description: East India Company director/chairman and British MP, named in the Bank of England's 1766 loan-extension record.

name: John Burgoyne
description: British MP who chaired a committee investigating Robert Clive's administration of the East India Company's affairs in India.

name: English Company Trading to the East Indies
description: New chartered corporation organized from government-debt subscribers in 1698; eventually united with the old East India Company. Not identical to the old Company before union.

name: General Society of East India subscribers
description: Chartered association of contributors to the Crown's 1698 two-million-pound public loan scheme, from which a new joint-stock East India trading company was formed.

name: South Sea Company
description: Chartered British company involved in government-debt financing and transatlantic trading rights, including commerce in enslaved Africans; subject of the 1720 speculative collapse.

name: William III of England
description: King whose government backed the 1694 Bank of England charter and pursued 1698 loans tied to East India trading privileges; original Bank stockholder.

name: Mary II of England
description: Queen and original Bank of England shareholder in 1694, with William III.

name: John Houblon
description: First Governor of the Bank of England when it was chartered in 1694.

name: Charles Montagu (Lord Halifax)
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer associated with the 1698 plan to raise £2 million in return for East India trade access.

name: John Aislabie
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer implicated in South Sea Company political corruption inquiries after the 1720 Bubble; precise personal transactions need archival examination.

name: Robert Walpole
description: British minister who advanced proposed redistribution of South Sea debt across the Bank of England and East India Company following the 1720 collapse; the planned engraftment was not carried out.

name: British silk and wool weavers protesting calico imports
description: Diverse London and regional craft groups protesting competition from imported Indian calico; some demonstrations included assaults against women wearing calico. Not a single centrally directed organization.

name: British Board of Trade
description: British state body that considered the East India Company's requests for compensating privileges during the 1721 calico controversy.

name: Michael Godfrey
description: Bank of England's first Deputy Governor, elected in July 1694 according to annual director lists; not identified as an East India or South Sea investor here.

name: Sir Henry Furnese
description: Named as among the Bank of England's first directors in July 1694; cross-company investment participation remains unverified.

name: John Law
description: Scottish financier who founded Banque Générale in France in 1716 and organized the Compagnie d'Occident; he became Controller General of Finances in 1720. His policy combined monetary innovation, government debt conversion and colonial-commercial privileges.

name: Philippe II, Duke of Orléans
description: Regent of France from 1715 who supported John Law's bank and chartered companies in attempts to reorganize French public finances.

name: French Crown under the Regency
description: French monarchy and regency authorities whose borrowing and colonial policies were intertwined with John Law's banking and trading arrangements.

name: Banque Générale
description: Privately established bank associated with John Law and circulating paper notes, later converted to royal control; it must not be conflated with a modern central bank.

name: Banque Royale
description: Successor phase of John Law's bank operating under royal authority and paper-note promises, associated with the monetary breakdown of 1720.

name: Compagnie d'Occident (Company of the West)
description: John Law's chartered French colonial trading corporation for Louisiana, later absorbed into the consolidated Compagnie des Indes.

name: Compagnie des Indes (French)
description: Consolidated French trading company under the Law system, with commercial, revenue and minting privileges that changed after the 1720 collapse. Distinct from the British East India Company.

name: Indigenous nations and communities of French Louisiana
description: Diverse Indigenous societies inhabiting the Mississippi watershed and neighboring lands before, during and after French colonization; this is a research category, not a single governing actor.

name: Enslaved Africans in French Louisiana
description: People trafficked and held in bondage as French colonial settlement and plantation schemes expanded; their experiences must not be reduced to projected company profits.

name: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville
description: French colonial officer involved in the choice of New Orleans' site in 1718, with help from Indigenous advisers.

name: Antoine Crozat
description: French financier who previously held Louisiana colonial trading rights before the Compagnie d'Occident; no role is inferred in later Law-era investor networks.

name: John Blunt
description: South Sea Company director and financier whose proposals for British public-debt conversion are discussed by economic historians; specific personal connections with John Law are not established.

name: Leydse Courant (Dutch newspaper)
description: Dutch newspaper whose surviving 1719–1721 images are made available in Yale's financial history project; do not infer a specific article's contents without reading that issue.

name: Share traders in Amsterdam, 1720
description: Descriptive category for financiers, brokers and investors, including an English coffee house depicted in contemporaneous satire. The category is not a uniform organization or a list of verified individuals.

name: Stad Rotterdam discount and lending company
description: Dutch Rotterdam discounting and lending institution whose original 1720–1723 journal, general ledger and transaction books are indexed by Yale's South Sea Bubble project.

name: Archibald Hutcheson
description: British parliamentarian and author of pamphlets questioning South Sea share valuations in 1720; a printed public letter is catalogued, but not proof of private correspondence with Law.

name: Diron (Louisiana colonial inspector)
description: Colonial administrative figure named as signer of the 1721 New Orleans census and author of a related letter dated January 2, 1722. First name and biography not established by this record.
